page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.64-1024 is a memory-dense compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The system features an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz, provisioned with 64 physical cores, dedicated allocation, and symmetric multithreading to deliver 128 vCPUs. Memory capacity totals 1024 GB of system RAM, presenting an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent data, and the instance includes no hardware accelerators or GPUs. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned by default.

Benchmark results show exceptional parallel computing throughput, placing the multi-core CPU score in the top ten percent alongside top-tier multi-threaded decompression results. Single-core performance and small-block cached memory bandwidth rank in the top quartile, supporting high transaction rates with Redis SET throughput exceeding 104 million operations per second. Uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth settle into the middle tier, as does single-threaded compression throughput.

Because local disk storage and GPU hardware are absent, raw cost efficiency is driven by the consolidation of CPU threads and memory capacity within a single virtual machine. This high memory-to-core ratio and robust multi-threaded compute density make the configuration well adapted for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, extensive multi-threaded ETL data pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning prompt processing.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.64-1024 is an x86_64 virtual server provisioned with 64 dedicated physical cores (128 vCPUs) using an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The instance is configured with 1024 GB of system RAM, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, but includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core processor performance and multi-threaded decompression, complemented by strong small-block cached memory bandwidth and high static web serving throughput. Uncached memory throughput remains moderate. The heavy allocation of memory alongside 128 virtual execution threads provides an efficient consolidation profile for large memory-bound enterprise applications, in-memory caches such as Redis, large-scale ETL pipelines, and multi-threaded data analytics workloads requiring substantial physical memory without requiring dedicated hardware accelerators.
